tk_hub_male_title: Ihram prohibitions for a male in ihram
tk_hub_female_title: Ihram prohibitions for a female in ihram
tk_ruling_detail: Details of the ruling and kaffarah:
tk_opt_forgetful: In the case of forgetfulness or ignorance
tk_opt_intentional: Deliberately, in a state of choice
tk_opt_necessity: Deliberately, in a state of necessity
tk_result_allowed_no_kaffara: It is permissible; there is no kaffarah
tk_m1_body1: It is not permissible for a man:
tk_m1_body2: To wear clothing whose parts are fastened together with buttons or anything else.
tk_m1_body3: Or to wear clothing in the manner of a shirt (qamis), so that the head and hands come out through openings made for them, i.e. the collar and sleeves.
tk_m1_body4: To wear trousers or similar clothing, such as pants, that cover both thighs; except when he does not have an izar (waist-wrapper) available.
tk_m1_body5: Also, based on obligatory precaution, wearing a shirt, robe, jubbah, jacket, or Arab clothing (thobe/dishdasha) like ordinary clothes, even if they are not worn in the usual way.
tk_m1_more1: If such clothing has already been put on, it should be removed in a way that the head is not covered.
tk_m1_more2: However, in that situation he may drape a shirt or similar garment over his shoulders, and wear a robe or similar without inserting his hands into the sleeves.
tk_m1_more3: None of these rulings depend on whether the garment is sewn, knitted, layered, or made in some other way.
tk_m1_kaffara_repeat: Give a separate goat as kaffarah for each time it was worn.
tk_m1_kaffara_many: If the garments worn are of different types, give a separate goat as kaffarah for each garment. If they are of the same type, then based on obligatory precaution there is still a separate goat as kaffarah for each garment.
tk_m1_necessity_body: If such clothing must be worn, remove it in a way that the head is not covered. Even in necessity, the kaffarah rulings still apply as a precaution.
tk_m2_title: Wearing something that covers the top of the foot
tk_m2_body1: For a man, wearing something that completely covers the upper part of the foot, such as shoes and socks.
tk_m2_note: Covering the top of the whole foot without wearing anything is permissible, for example draping the edge of one's ihram cloth over the feet while sitting.
tk_m2_more1: Wearing a shoe is problematic for a man in ihram if only the toes are visible; that is, some of the upper foot besides the toes should remain uncovered.
tk_m2_more2: Covering a prosthetic foot with a sock or anything else is not permissible.
tk_m2_more3: A man in ihram may use a sock that does not cover the instep, though the precaution is not to use it either.
tk_m2_example: Example: he cannot find open sandals and needs to wear covering shoes.
tk_m2_haram_body: Based on obligatory precaution, it is permissible to wear shoes or socks that cover the top of the foot after tearing them.
tk_m2_kaffara_body1: There is no kaffarah for wearing shoes.
tk_m2_kaffara_body2: Based on obligatory precaution, wearing socks and the like has a kaffarah of one goat, whether worn by choice or out of necessity.
tk_m3_body1: Covering the head or any part of it with a niqab, head-covering, cloth, or anything similar.
tk_m3_note: “Head” means the area where hair grows, and the ears are included. So using a phone in a way that covers the ear counts as covering the head; details follow.
tk_m3_more1: The ruling of covering the head applies only to men, and includes the head and both ears.
tk_m3_more2: If a sewn cloth is on the head, such as a cap, there is kaffarah for it; other sewn clothing is a separate issue from covering the head.
tk_m3_opt_cloth: Covering the head with a niqab, head-covering, or cloth
tk_m3_opt_object: Covering the head by placing soil, grass, or something else on it
tk_m3_opt_phone: Covering the ear with a mobile phone
tk_m3_opt_towel: Drying the head with a handkerchief or towel
tk_m3_opt_airplane: Covering the head because of baldness, a bandage, or on a plane
tk_m3_opt_wig: Covering the head with a wig
tk_m3_cloth_body: Deliberately covering the head with cloth while having a choice is haram, and there is kaffarah for it.
tk_m3_object_body: Covering the head by placing something on it also has the ruling of covering the head.
tk_m3_phone_body: Holding a phone to the ear so that the ear is covered has the ruling of covering the head.
tk_m3_towel_body: Drying the head with a handkerchief or towel has the same ruling if the head becomes covered.
tk_m3_airplane_body: The following cases are permitted for a man in ihram where there is need, while still observing precaution.
tk_m3_wig_body: Covering the head with a wig also has the ruling of covering the head.
tk_m4_body1: A man walking under moving (non-fixed) shade to avoid the sun, and, based on obligatory precaution, to avoid rain.
tk_m4_note: It is permissible for pre-pubescent children to walk under moving shade.
tk_m4_more1: If it is possible to stop the vehicle or get out: it is obligatory to stop or get out until the rain ends. If getting out or stopping is not possible in any way, then there is neither sin nor kaffarah.
tk_m4_more2: If the vehicle is not stopped or left in order to avoid expected harm, for example fearing a traffic violation, then there is no sin, but one goat is due as kaffarah.
tk_m4_more3: Note: if this happens several times in the same ihram, one kaffarah is enough, though recommended precaution is a separate kaffarah for each day.
tk_m4_opt_sun: Walking under moving shade to avoid sun or rain, with the shading object over the head
tk_m4_opt_vehicle: The shading object being over the vehicle (while riding)
tk_m4_opt_night: Rain starting suddenly during night travel
tk_m4_sun_body: Deliberately taking shade is haram, and there is kaffarah for it.
tk_m4_vehicle_body: Traveling under the roof of a vehicle has the ruling of moving shade.
tk_m4_night_body: If rain starts suddenly at night and the vehicle cannot be stopped, there is neither sin nor kaffarah.
tk_m5_title: Contracting a marriage or being present at it
tk_m5_body1: It is haram for a person in ihram to recite his own or someone else's marriage contract.
tk_m5_body2: Based on obligatory precaution, being a witness to the marriage contract and being present when it is concluded, whether the other person is in ihram or not, and whether the marriage is permanent or temporary (mut'ah).
tk_m5_note: It is recommended to avoid giving testimony about a marriage contract even if that testimony was obtained before ihram.
tk_m5_opt_read: Reciting one's own or someone else's marriage contract
tk_m5_opt_witness: Based on obligatory precaution, witnessing the contract or being present at it
tk_m5_read_body: It is haram. If the one who recites the contract is a man, the kaffarah is one goat, provided that one of the two parties knew. This ruling does not apply to someone who was unaware.
tk_m5_witness_body: Based on obligatory precaution, being present at the contract or witnessing it should be avoided. Kaffarah is not obligatory.
tk_m6_body1: A man having vaginal or anal intercourse while in ihram out of forgetfulness or ignorance.
tk_m6_intentional_body: The umrah is valid. However, if intercourse occurred before sa'i, the umrah becomes invalid and the kaffarah is a camel. If it occurred after sa'i, the umrah remains valid and the kaffarah is still a camel.
tk_m7_body1: A man kissing his wife while in ihram.
tk_m7_opt_affection: Kissing out of affection or fondness
tk_m7_lust_body: It is haram, and there is kaffarah for it.
tk_m7_no_lust_body: It is not permissible. If semen is not emitted from looking or kissing, there is no kaffarah.
tk_m7_affection_body: Kissing out of affection or fondness should also be avoided as a precaution.
tk_m8_title: Touching, lifting, or holding one's wife
tk_m8_body1: A man in ihram touching, lifting, or embracing his wife.
tk_m8_more1: If he touches with lust there is kaffarah; without lust there is no kaffarah (Mas'alah 228).
tk_m8_opt_crowd: Catching a woman who is falling in a severe tawaf crowd
tk_m8_opt_joke: Being touched, i.e. one's wife touching him
tk_m8_lust_body: Touching with lust is haram, and there is kaffarah for it.
tk_m8_no_lust_body: There is no kaffarah for touching without lust, but it should be avoided as a precaution.
tk_m9_body1: A man looking at his wife while in ihram and playing with her is haram in some cases.
tk_m9_note: Talking with one's wife other than whispering, and similar acts, are permissible. Recommended precaution is to avoid taking any kind of pleasure from her.
tk_m9_lust_body: Looking with lust is haram. If semen is emitted, there is kaffarah.
tk_m10_body1: Masturbation while in ihram (i.e. causing ejaculation).
tk_m10_opt_rub: By rubbing the penis with the hand or the like
tk_m10_opt_wife_think: By arousing thoughts of one's wife
tk_m10_opt_imagine: By hearing a woman's words or description, or imagining her
tk_m10_opt_arouse: By any act that arouses lust, such as pressure on the prostate
tk_m10_intentional_body: If it happens before sa'i, the umrah becomes invalid and, based on obligatory precaution, the kaffarah is a camel. After sa'i the umrah is valid and the kaffarah is a camel.
tk_m11_body1: Using perfume in ihram. Perfume means anything used to scent the body, clothes, food, or anything else, such as musk, amber, wars (safflower/camphor), saffron, and the like. Common perfumes are also included, such as rose, jasmine, and similar scents.
tk_m11_note: Whether the scent is plant-based, animal-based, or petroleum-based, it counts as perfume.
tk_m11_more2: Wearing clothing that has a scent of perfume.
tk_m11_opt_wear: Wearing clothing that has a scent of perfume
tk_m11_opt_mask: Using a mask to avoid a bad smell
tk_m11_use_body: Using perfume deliberately is haram, and there is kaffarah for it.
tk_m11_mask_body: Using a mask to avoid a bad smell is permissible, provided it is not a scented mask.
tk_m12_body1: For a man or woman in ihram, deliberately using anything commonly regarded as adornment is haram based on obligatory precaution, whether or not there is an intention to adorn.
tk_m12_note: This is one of the prohibitions for which there is no kaffarah in any case, whether by forgetfulness, ignorance, or deliberately.
tk_m12_henna_body: Applying henna for adornment should be avoided based on obligatory precaution. There is no kaffarah.
tk_m12_ring_body: Wearing a ring for adornment should be avoided as a precaution.
tk_m12_glasses_body: If the glasses are so dark that the eyes and the area around them appear adorned, they should be avoided as a precaution.
tk_m12_jewelry_body: Wearing jewelry has the ruling of adornment; there is no kaffarah.
tk_m13_body1: A man or woman applying kohl to the eyes while in ihram.
tk_m13_black_body: Applying kohl for adornment is haram; there is no kaffarah.
tk_m13_medicine_body: If needed for treatment, it is permissible.
tk_m14_body1: A man or woman in ihram looking in a mirror for adornment.
tk_m14_opt_adorn: Looking in a mirror for adornment
tk_m14_opt_need: For a need (for example checking a wound)
tk_m14_adorn_body: Looking in a mirror for adornment is haram; there is no kaffarah.
tk_m14_need_body: Looking in a mirror for a need is permissible.
tk_m15_body1: A man or woman in ihram applying oil.
tk_m15_scented_body: Applying scented oil has the ruling of perfume, and there is kaffarah for it.
tk_m15_plain_body: Unscented oil should be avoided based on obligatory precaution.
tk_m15_medicine_body: If needed for treatment, it is permissible.
tk_m16_body1: A man or woman in ihram removing hair. Meaning: a person in ihram shaving or plucking hair from one's own body or from someone else's.
tk_m16_note: Hair falling during wudu, ghusl, tayammum, or in any other way, including hair falling for wudu or ghusl, is not a problem.
tk_m16_opt_stroke: Running the hand through the hair without purpose
tk_m16_opt_hijab: Hair coming out when removing a headscarf
tk_m16_own_body: Deliberately removing one's own hair is haram, and there is kaffarah for it.
tk_m16_other_body: It is not permissible, whether the other person is in ihram or not.
tk_m16_comb_body: If combing pulls out hair, it should be avoided.
tk_m16_stroke_body: If running the hand through the hair pulls hair out, it should be avoided as a precaution.
tk_m16_hijab_body: If she knows that hair will come out when removing the headscarf, she should take precaution.
tk_m17_body1: A man or woman in ihram killing insects on the body or clothes.
tk_m17_kill_body: Deliberately killing insects is haram; in some cases there is kaffarah.
tk_m17_remove_body: Removing or driving them away is permissible, though recommended precaution is not to do so.
tk_m18_body1: A man or woman in ihram drawing blood from the body is, based on precaution, [prohibited], even by scratching.
tk_m18_note: Using a miswak or brush is not a problem if blood comes out, so long as the intention is not to draw blood.
tk_m18_opt_bleed: Drawing blood by cupping, phlebotomy, or similar
tk_m18_bleed_body: Deliberately drawing blood is haram based on obligatory precaution; there is no kaffarah.
tk_m19_body1: A person in ihram cutting nails.
tk_m19_one_body: The kaffarah for each nail is one mudd of food.
tk_m19_all_body: Cutting all the nails of the hands and feet has a kaffarah of one goat.
tk_m20_body1: A person in ihram washing the head in a way that hair is broken.
tk_m20_soap_body: Washing the head with soap is haram if it pulls out hair or if it is scented.
tk_m20_water_body: Washing with water only is permissible if it does not pull out hair.
tk_m21_body1: A man or woman in ihram lying, using abusive language, or showing forbidden pride.
tk_m21_note: Forbidden pride means boasting before others about one's family, wealth, rank, or the like, when it includes insulting a believer and lowering his honor.
tk_m21_lie_body: Lying is haram; there is no kaffarah, but one should seek forgiveness as a precaution.
tk_m21_pride_body: Showing forbidden pride should be avoided.
tk_m22_body1: Argument (disputation). Meaning: a debate in which one swears by Allah when reporting that something is or is not the case. The oath by Allah may use the word “Allah” or another of His names, in Arabic or another language.
tk_m22_note_item1: This ruling does not apply to swearing by a sacred being or thing other than Allah.
tk_m22_note_item2: Likewise, if an oath by Allah is taken for a purpose other than reporting news, this ruling does not apply.
tk_m22_true_body: There is kaffarah for swearing a true oath several times, for example three times.
tk_m22_false_body: Swearing a false oath is haram, and there is kaffarah for it.
tk_m23_body1: A man or woman in ihram wearing or carrying weapons. Weapon means anything commonly called a weapon, such as a sword, gun, or spear. Defensive equipment is not included, such as armor, a helmet, and the like.
tk_m23_opt_carry: Carrying a weapon in a way that one is commonly considered armed
tk_m23_opt_keep: Keeping a weapon, or carrying it in a way that one is not commonly considered armed
tk_m23_wear_body: Wearing a weapon is haram; it is permissible in a case of fear.
tk_m23_carry_body: Carrying a weapon in a way that one is commonly considered armed is haram.
tk_m23_keep_body: If one is not commonly considered armed, it is permissible.
tk_m24_body1: Hunting a wild land animal or its young, or considering hunting lawful. This is haram for a person in ihram, whether done deliberately, forgetfully, or out of not knowing the ruling.
tk_m24_body2: Hunting includes: hunting, killing, wounding, breaking a limb, and causing any kind of harm.
tk_m24_body3: In addition, the following are also haram:
tk_m24_body4: Helping in the hunt, even by pointing.
tk_m24_body5: Keeping a hunted animal, whether one hunted it oneself or someone else did, and whether it was hunted inside or outside the Haram.
tk_m24_body6: Eating the meat of a hunted animal, even if a person not in ihram hunted it outside the Haram.
tk_m24_body7: Taking, breaking, or eating the eggs of a wild animal, and, based on obligatory precaution, helping in these acts.
tk_m24_note: 1. A wild animal is one that by nature flees from humans, even if it has become tame for some reason. There is no difference between lawful-meat and unlawful-meat animals. Fish are also included. 2. These acts are also haram inside the Haram for someone not in ihram.
tk_m24_land_body: The kaffarah for hunting a wild land animal is according to its equivalent.
tk_m24_bird_body: The kaffarah for hunting pigeons and similar birds is one goat or its value.
tk_m24_locust_body: The kaffarah for killing a locust is one mudd of food.
tk_m24_bee_body: The kaffarah for killing a wasp is a handful of dates or similar food.
tk_m24_other_body: The kaffarah for other animals is according to their equivalent.
tk_f1_body1: It is not permissible for a woman in ihram to cover her face with a burqa, niqab, a hand-fan, or anything similar. Obligatory precaution is not to cover the face with anything at all.
tk_f1_note: Covering the face while sleeping is permissible.
tk_f1_more1: In the ordinary case, a burqa or niqab is not permissible.
tk_f1_more2: If a niqab is tied so that the cloth is held up in line with the nose, it is not required [in that manner].
tk_f1_more3: Obligatory precaution is that no part of the face should be covered either.
tk_f1_more4: If glasses are so dark that the eyes and the area around them are concealed, they should be avoided as a precaution.
tk_f1_more5: The precaution is not to do so, even if it is only wiping.
tk_f1_full_body: Deliberately covering the whole face while having a choice is haram; the kaffarah is one goat.
tk_f1_part_body: Covering part of the face should also be avoided based on obligatory precaution.
tk_f2_body1: A woman in ihram wearing gloves on her hands.
tk_f2_no_need_body: Wearing gloves deliberately is haram; there is no kaffarah.
tk_f2_need_body: Wearing them out of necessity is permissible.
tk_f7_body1: A woman in ihram playing with a man.
tk_f7_husband_body: Looking at one's husband with lust is haram.
tk_f7_no_lust_body: There is no kaffarah for it, even if semen is emitted from looking.
